components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single strongest action in a task area, with quiet lift and an explicit focus ring.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary">Continue to review<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 12h14M13 6l6 6-6 6"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; min-height:44px; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:8px; border:0; border-radius:8px; background:var(--primary, #276221); color:#fff; padding:8px 16px; font-family:var(--font-sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); font-size:14px; font-weight:600; box-shadow:0 5px 14px rgba(39,98,33,.14); cursor:pointer; transition:background-color 150ms ease, transform 150ms ease, box-shadow 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary svg { width:16px; height:16px; fill:none; stroke:currentColor; stroke-width:2; stroke-linecap:round; stroke-linejoin:round; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:var(--primary-hover, #1f531b); transform:translateY(-1px); box-shadow:0 7px 18px rgba(39,98,33,.18); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform:translateY(0); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid rgba(70,146,60,.35); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A supportive action that stays visually inside the green paper system.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display:inline-flex; min-height:40px; align-items:center; justify-content:center; border:0; border-radius:8px; background:var(--muted-bg, #edf4eb); color:var(--primary, #276221); padding:8px 16px; font-family:var(--font-sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); font-size:14px; font-weight:600; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background:#dfeedd; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { background:#d8ead5; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid rgba(70,146,60,.3); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: A contained low-emphasis action for pairing with a primary button.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display:inline-flex; min-height:40px; align-items:center; justify-content:center; border:1px solid #cfdccc; border-radius:8px; background:#fff; color:#365134; padding:8px 16px; font-family:var(--font-sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); font-size:14px; font-weight:600; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color 150ms ease, border-color 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background:#f3f7f1; border-color:#bdd2b9; } .ds-btn-outline:active { background:#edf4eb; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline:2px solid rgba(70,146,60,.3); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: A plain-language field with a strong, broad focus treatment.

narrative.overview:
CaseLink should feel like a well-prepared folder passed between trusted colleagues: ordered, legible, and ready for the next responsible action. The interface uses warm paper fields, crisp white working surfaces, quiet green structure, and concise language so a school case manager can move from family intake to reviewed plan to paperwork without needing software expertise.

Polish comes from proportion, steady alignment, and visible review boundaries—not visual spectacle. Public surfaces are spacious and reassuring; the authenticated workspace is denser and more operational. Both share the same restrained green palette, Geist Sans, gently curved geometry, and explicit human-control cues.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper surroundings with white working surfaces
Deep green reserved for action, location, and completion
Compact controls inside generous page-level spacing
Clear provenance, review state, and manual handoff language
Motion that confirms interaction without turning AI into spectacle

rules.name: The Verdant Restraint Rule
rules.body: Forest Action Green marks the next action, current location, or a purposeful public emphasis; it does not flood routine working surfaces.

rules.name: The Written State Rule
rules.body: Review, success, and error colors always travel with plain-language labels or icons; color is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Plainspoken Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Type communicates order without jargon: one decisive heading, direct supporting copy, and labels written for school staff rather than software specialists.

rules.name: The Room Around the Work Rule
rules.body: Give the page generous breathing room, then make controls and review rows compact enough for daily operations; do not solve density by stacking decorative cards.

rules.name: The Lift With Purpose Rule
rules.body: A shadow must explain hierarchy or response; routine cards rely on paper contrast and a one-pixel border.

rules.name: The Quiet Curve Rule
rules.body: Corners soften institutional workflows without making them playful; preserve the control, card, feature, and pill hierarchy instead of rounding every element to the maximum.

rules.name: The Visible Handoff Rule
rules.body: AI-prepared values remain editable and traceable, attention states remain visible, and no completion treatment implies automatic submission.

dos: Do reserve Forest Action Green for primary actions, active location, and meaningful completion.
Do place white working surfaces on Warm Paper or green-tinted page fields.
Do keep provenance, review status, and the next human action visible in paperwork flows.
Do use plain labels, readable focus rings, and words or icons alongside semantic color.
Do pair generous page spacing with compact operational controls.
donts: Don't reintroduce blue or slate as a competing primary visual system; migrate remaining legacy primitives into the green palette when touched.
Don't use gradients, decorative AI glow, or excessive floating cards to imply sophistication.
Don't turn the Families workspace into an analytics dashboard or add charts without a decision-making need.
Don't imply direct CitySpan integration, automatic submission, or AI authority over case-manager judgment.
Don't use identifiable family details in public previews or demonstration fixtures.
